subject: Clarify reserved GPU pool sizing, throughput measurement & SLA language — Zephyr Therapeutics
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@zephyrtx.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@zephyrtx.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0400
Subject: Reserved pool commit — need clarity on throughput units and discount triggers

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo this week. We're pushing this through procurement and legal and a few items came up we need clarified before we can sign:

1) How do you define the committed "capacity unit"? Is it a GPU-hour, vGPU slice, or a throughput-based unit (tokens/sec or requests/sec)?

2) If actual utilization is lower across the month, do we get credits or a pro-rated discount? Our CFO wants guarantees how the discounted rate ties to measured usage.

3) We also need to understand the measurement window and the telemetry you use to compute SLA or utilization numbers (UTC vs customer local time, 5-min vs 15-min aggregation).

I attached our internal SOW with proposed commit numbers. Can you confirm the definitions in the contract redline so procurement can complete their review?

Alex Turner
Head of AI Ops, Zephyr Therapeutics
alex.turner@zephyrtx.com
+1 415-555-0188

Attachments: Zephyr_SOW_RevA.pdf (PDF)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@zephyrtx.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved pool commit — need clarity on throughput units and discount triggers

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Below is how Redwood defines and measures the pieces referenced in the SOW; I also attached a draft redline that maps these to contract language.

Summary (short):
- Capacity unit: we define a "Capacity Unit (CU)" as a reserved GPU-minute equivalent tied to a named GPU class (e.g., A100-80GB CU). CU billing and commit are denominated in GPU-minutes per billing month.
- Throughput guarantee: our throughput SLA is measured in "aggregate RPS-equivalent tokens/sec" per committed pool, normalized for model family and sequence length using our kernel-profiled conversion.
- Measurement window: we compute utilization on 5-minute rolling windows aggregated UTC, with monthly averaging used to determine utilization tiers for discounts or credits.

Key contract redline highlights (in attached doc):
1) Definition of CU: "A Capacity Unit (CU) equals 60 GPU-minutes on the Reserved GPU Class listed in Appendix A. Customer may map multiple CU types to model variants; Redwood will publish conversion factors."
2) Throughput measurement: "Throughput shall be measured as median tokens/second across 5-minute windows per pool, adjusted by model profile conversion factors. Measurement is UTC time."
3) Underutilization credits: "If average monthly utilization falls below 65% of committed CUs, Customer shall be eligible for a pro-rated credit equal to 50% of the unused CU spend, applied to the subsequent invoice period, subject to a minimum administrative threshold of $1,000."
4) SLA/service credit: "Service credits are calculated as a percentage of monthly committed spend when availability SLOs are not met. Credits will not exceed 100% of monthly committed fees."

I'll flag Marissa on the redline language for legal standards and Rishi on the conversion math. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk procurement through the telemetry.

Best,
Olga Petrov

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved pool commit — suggested legal redlines (service credit table attached)

Alex / Olga — looping in a short legal & commercial redline. A few items we edited for procurement comfort:

- We tightened the CU definition to explicitly reference Appendix A hardware classes and included a clause for "conversion factors" to avoid ambiguity when Zephyr runs different model families.
- For credits, procurement preferred a simpler calculation: unused CU credit = (Committed CU minutes - Billed CU minutes) * Effective CU rate * 0.50, with a monthly floor as previously proposed. I've added an example in the attached spreadsheet.
- For SLA remedies, we propose a stepped credit schedule: 2% credit for <99.5% availability, 5% for <99%, 15% for <95%, with a 100% cap for catastrophic failure. Credits apply to committed spend only.
- Exclusions: maintenance windows and force majeure per standard terms.

We used conservative language around measurement (UTC, 5-min windows) but left a clause allowing for joint-audit if Zephyr disagrees with conversion factors. That joint-audit path is limited to once per 12 months and costs borne by the losing party.

I've attached SLA_ServiceCredit_Table.xlsx and incorporated the redline in the DOCX. Please review and let me know if the stepped remedy schedule works for you.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: SLA_ServiceCredit_Table.xlsx (XLSX); RI_Dedicated_Commit_Definitions_redline.docx (DOCX)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2027 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved pool commit — throughput normalization details

Quick technical note from infra:

- Conversion factors: we normalize using a small suite of microbenchmarks (tokenization + attention + MLP) per model family. Those factors are published as a number (e.g., A100-80GB -> GPT2-xl = 1.0, Llama2-70B = 0.85) and are applied to raw tokens/sec to produce "RPS-equivalent tokens/sec" used in contractual measurement.
- Burst behavior: reserved pools support short bursts beyond committed CU if spare capacity exists in the cluster; bursts are measured and billed separately as "overage minutes" at the API rate. Bursts do not reduce committed CU credits.
- Telemetry: usage and health metrics are retained for 12 months by default and can be exported by customer for audits. We record per-5-minute sample values as UTC epoch and keep medians for billing.

If Zephyr wants, we can expose a read-only Prometheus endpoint (or CloudWatch metrics via integration) during the initial 90-day ramp so procurement can validate numbers before invoicing.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

1) Can we get the conversion-factor microbenchmark report (just results, not tooling) for the three model families we expect to use?
2) Please add a clause that credits are applied within 45 days of the invoice following the month where the shortfall occurred.

If you can confirm those two items, I'll schedule a final 30-min call with procurement for Thursday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alex
